record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: Let α_r(Γ) be the maximum size of an r-independent set in a continuous graph Γ, and let β_r(Γ) be the minimum number of radius-r balls needed to cover all points of Γ. For a continuous graph Γ with n endpoint vertices and a radius r > 0, what upper or lower bounds can one give for α_r(Γ) + β_r(Γ) as a function of n and r, and can such bounds be made tight?

evidence.quote: Definition 10. Given a positive real number r, a set of balls B = {B(p, r) : p ∈ E} is called an r-cover of Γ if for any point q ∈ E there is a ball B ∈ B containing q. The r-cover number of Γ is the cardinality of the minimum r-cover in Γ further denoted as βr(Γ) or βr for simplicity.
In general, the following question can be addressed: Given r > 0, what is the bound on αr(Γ) + βr(Γ) for a continuous graph Γ in terms of n and r? Is the bound tight?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A continuous graph $\Gamma$ is a topological space obtained from a finite multigraph by realizing each edge as a closed arc isometric to a real interval, so that $\Gamma$ becomes a compact metric space (with the path-length metric); the $n$ vertices of the underlying multigraph are called the endpoint vertices of $\Gamma$, and points of $\Gamma$ include all interior points of the edges. For a real number $r>0$ and a point $p\in\Gamma$, let $B(p,r)=\{q\in\Gamma:d(p,q)\le r\}$ denote the closed ball of radius $r$ in $\Gamma$.

Define:
- An $r$-independent set in $\Gamma$ is a subset $S\subseteq\Gamma$ such that $d(p,q)>r$ for all distinct $p,q\in S$. Let $\alpha_r(\Gamma)$ be the supremum of $|S|$ over all $r$-independent sets $S$.
- An $r$-cover of $\Gamma$ is a collection of closed balls $\{B(p_i,r)\}_{i\in I}$ with $p_i\in\Gamma$ whose union equals $\Gamma$. Let $\beta_r(\Gamma)$ be the minimum cardinality of an $r$-cover of $\Gamma$.

Problem. Given a continuous graph $\Gamma$ with $n$ endpoint vertices and a radius $r>0$, determine upper and lower bounds for the sum
$$\alpha_r(\Gamma)+\beta_r(\Gamma)$$
as a function of $n$ and $r$, and decide whether such bounds can be made tight (i.e., attained by some continuous graph).
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the duality bound for $\alpha_r(\Gamma)+\beta_r(\Gamma)$ on continuous graphs in terms of $n$ and $r$ was located. The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on combinatorial properties of continuous graphs, and standard literature on independence/covering duality does not address this metric/continuous-graph version.

status_evidence.title: Independent set (graph theory) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Standard combinatorial independence/covering duality is the discrete Gallai-type identity; no analogue is given for continuous (metric) graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existing duality results address discrete graphs, not continuous graphs with radius-r balls.

status_evidence.title: Independence Number -- Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Defines the independence number for finite graphs without reference to metric/continuous analogues.
status_evidence.claim: No bound for the metric version on continuous graphs is reported.
